ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the line $y_1=x+b$ intersects with $y_2=kx-1$ at point P. What is the solution set of the inequality $x+b>kx-1$ with respect to $x$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} From the graph, we know that the coordinates of the intersection point of the two lines are $\left(-1, \frac{1}{2}\right)$. Additionally, when $x > -1$, the graph of the function $y = x + b$ is above the graph of the function $y = kx - 1$,\\
$\therefore$ the solution set for the inequality in terms of $x$, $x + b > kx - 1$, is $x > -1$.\\
Therefore, the answer is: $\boxed{x > -1}$.
